title: 504. The French Revolution: War to the Death (Part 2)

sentences.en: The audacious satellites of despotism, carrying 15 centuries of pride and barbarism in their
sentences.zh: 专制暴政厚颜无耻的帮凶，灵魂中烙印着长达十五个世纪的傲慢与野蛮，

sentences.en: feudal souls, are now demanding in every land and from every throne the golden soldiers to reconquer the scepter of France.
sentences.zh: 如今正在每一片土地、每一座王座前叫嚣，索要黄金勇士以重夺法兰西的权杖。

sentences.en: You have shaken off the yoke of your despots, but surely this was not to bend the knee before a foreign tyrant.
sentences.zh: 你们已经甩脱了暴君的枷锁，但绝不是为了在异国暴君面前屈膝下跪。

sentences.en: So now, led by the most sublime passions,
sentences.zh: 所以现在，在最崇高激昂的热情引领下，

sentences.en: beneath the tricolor flag that you gloriously planted on the ruins of the Bastille.
sentences.zh: 在你们光荣插在巴士底狱废墟上的三色旗下，

sentences.en: Follow the course of your great destiny that beckons you on to the punishment of tyrants.
sentences.zh: 顺应你们伟大命运的召唤，去惩罚那些暴君吧。

sentences.en: Union et courage.
sentences.zh: 团结与勇气。

sentences.en: Glory awaits you.
sentences.zh: 荣耀等待着你们。

sentences.en: To arMs. To arMs. The honour and the salvation of the nation demand it.
sentences.zh: 拿起武器！拿起武器！为了国家的荣誉与拯救，必须如此。

sentences.en: To arMs. To arMs. So that, Dominic, was exceptionally rousing rhetoric, I think.
sentences.zh: 拿起武器！拿起武器！所以，多米尼克，这段修辞真是精彩得无以复加。

sentences.en: Brilliantly, renterloquized by me.
sentences.zh: 由我精彩地朗诵出来。

sentences.en: Par moi.
sentences.zh: 用法语。

sentences.en: And it was Pierre Venio who was addressing the
sentences.zh: 当时向巴黎

sentences.en: Legislative Assembly in Paris on the 3rd of January 1792.
sentences.zh: 立法议会发表讲话的是皮埃尔·韦尼奥，时间是1792年1月3日。

sentences.en: And what he was doing there was saying, let's have a crack at the Austrians.
sentences.zh: 而他当时的意思是，咱们去跟奥地利人较量一下吧。

sentences.en: He was indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So Venio was a brilliant speaker.
sentences.zh: 所以韦尼奥是个极其出色的演说家。

sentences.en: Well, as listeners will be able to tell from that rendition.
sentences.zh: 听众从刚才那段演绎里就能听出来。

sentences.en: I mean, that was very rousing, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那真的非常振奋人心，汤姆。

sentences.en: If I were a Frenchman, I'd be on my feet.
sentences.zh: 如果我是个法国人，我早就起立欢呼了。

sentences.en: Should we go and invade Vienna?
sentences.zh: 我们要不要去攻打维也纳？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So he was thought of as the best orator of the entire French Revolution.
sentences.zh: 因此他被认为是整个法国大革命中最伟大的演说家。

sentences.en: The Cicero of the Republic.
sentences.zh: 共和国的西塞罗。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We haven't mentioned him before, but he was one of the leading lights in a new faction, which will appear in today's episode.
sentences.zh: 我们以前没提过他，但他是新派系中的核心人物之一，这派系将在今天的节目中登场。

sentences.en: Waves of factions, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 派系真是一波接一波，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: We've got factions.
sentences.zh: 我们有派系。

sentences.en: We've got so many factions.
sentences.zh: 我们有太多的派系了。

sentences.en: So they were called the Girondins, and they're really the party of war.
sentences.zh: 他们被称为吉伦特派，实际上可以说是战争党。

sentences.en: And this is going to be a transformative moment in this whole story, and will change the course of the revolution completely,
sentences.zh: 这将是整个故事中具有变革意义的时刻，并将彻底改变革命的进程，

sentences.en: but not merely a transformative moment for the French Revolution.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅对法国大革命具有变革意义。

sentences.en: This is a transformative moment in world history, because this is the beginning of a war that they all think, everybody thinks, will be home by Christmas.
sentences.zh: 这也是世界历史上的一个变革时刻，因为这是一场他们所有人都认为——每个人都认为——能在圣诞节前结束的战争的开端。

sentences.en: And actually, it lasts for almost 25 years off and on, totally redraws the map of Europe, and costs millions of lives.
sentences.zh: 而实际上，这场战争断断续续持续了将近25年，彻底重绘了欧洲地图，并夺去了数百万人的生命。

sentences.en: It's not just Europe, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实不仅仅是欧洲。

sentences.en: It's a genuine world war.
sentences.zh: 这是一场真正的世界大战。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So this is the road to Waterloo.
sentences.zh: 所以这是通往滑铁卢之路。

sentences.en: It is the road to Waterloo.
sentences.zh: 这就是通往滑铁卢之路。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's how we should brand this series.
sentences.zh: 我们应该这样给这个系列冠名。

sentences.en: It's the road to Waterloo.
sentences.zh: 这就是通往滑铁卢之路。

sentences.en: And nobody in the Assembly that day, listening to Venio speak, has the slightest semblance of an inkling of what is coming.
sentences.zh: 当时议会里听韦尼奥演讲的任何人，都没有哪怕一丝一毫对即将到来的一切的预感。

sentences.en: Because what people often think about the First World War, that people went to war with great enthusiasm, and hurrah, and let's do it.
sentences.zh: 因为人们对第一次世界大战常有一种看法，即人们带着极大的热情、欢呼和冲劲奔赴战场。

sentences.en: This is actually true of this, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这其实也适用于这次，对吧？

sentences.en: There's great enthusiasm for it.
sentences.zh: 大家对它充满了热情。

sentences.en: Far more so.
sentences.zh: 有过之而无不及。

sentences.en: I mean, there's none of the foreboding that you have in the roads to the First World War.
sentences.zh: 我是说，完全没有那种通往一战道路上的厄运预感。

sentences.en: There is none of the sense of apocalyptic doom.
sentences.zh: 没有任何末日降临的感觉。

sentences.en: Well, there is a sense of apocalypse, I think.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得还是有一种末日感的。

sentences.en: A sense that good and evil will be engaged in a titanic confrontation, and that the forces of good will triumph.
sentences.zh: 一种善恶将展开惊天对决、且正义终将战胜邪恶的感觉。

sentences.en: And that is what is animating Venio's language.
sentences.zh: 这就是赋予韦尼奥言辞灵魂的东西。

sentences.en: I mean, he thinks of himself as a Cicero, but he is also absolutely part of that kind of apocalyptic Christian tradition.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他自诩为西塞罗，但他绝对也是那种具有末日色彩的基督教传统的一部分。

sentences.en: You're not wrong, Tom.
sentences.zh: 你没说错，汤姆。

sentences.en: You're never wrong when you bring out the, being part of a Christian continuity, are you?
sentences.zh: 每当你扯到基督教精神的延续性时，你从没错过，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, but it's the fusion of the classical and the Christian, I think, does so much to explain what makes this revolutionary tradition so instantaneously potent.
sentences.zh: 对，但我觉得正是古典主义和基督教的融合，在很大程度上解释了为什么这个革命传统能具有如此即时的爆发力。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think you're right.
sentences.zh: 对，我想你是对的。

sentences.en: Talk about it being new, and it is, the sense of novelty is part of the excitement, but it's a novelty that people have been conditioned to accept.
sentences.zh: 说到它的新颖性，确实如此，这种新鲜感正是兴奋点的一部分，但这是一种人们已经被训练去接受的新颖性。

sentences.en: So how do we get there?
sentences.zh: 那么我们是如何走到这一步的？

sentences.en: How do we get to war?
sentences.zh: 我们是怎么走向战争的？

sentences.en: Well, remember where we ended last time.
sentences.zh: 好吧，回想一下我们上次节目结束的地方。

sentences.en: We ended on the 30th of September, 1791.
sentences.zh: 我们的时间定格在1791年9月30日。

sentences.en: The Constitution has been agreed.
sentences.zh: 宪法已经通过。

sentences.en: The National Assembly has met for the last time and gone home.
sentences.zh: 国民议会召开最后一次会议后解散回家。

sentences.en: And Louis has promised to knuckle down as a constitutional monarch, a promise that, as everybody listening to these podcasts will know, he fully intends to break.
sentences.zh: 路易也承诺要踏踏实实做一个立宪君主——正如所有收听这些播客的人所知，他压根儿没打算遵守这个承诺。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the great revolutionary club, the Jacquemin club, has split into two.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，伟大的革命俱乐部雅各宾俱乐部一分为二。

sentences.en: The moderates have all walked out and set up their Foyant club under Antoine Barnave and his friends, who appear to be the people in charge.
sentences.zh: 温和派全部退党，在安托万·巴纳夫及其朋友们的带领下成立了斐扬俱乐部，他们似乎成了掌权者。

sentences.en: And that has left the Jacquemin as a kind of rump club, and its big star is Maximilien Robespierre.
sentences.zh: 这使得雅各宾派变成了一个类似残余的俱乐部，而它最大的明星是马克西米连·罗伯斯庇尔。
zh_words: 马克西米连·罗伯斯庇尔

sentences.en: So let's pick up straight away.
sentences.zh: 那我们直接接着往下讲。

sentences.en: The new assembly voted for by sort of taxpayers, property owners, meets for the first time at the beginning of October.
sentences.zh: 由各类纳税人和业主投票产生的新议会在10月初首次召开。

sentences.en: So 742 members, and they're all new people, because the old people have said they're not going to stand for the new assembly.
sentences.zh: 共有742名成员，而且全都是新面孔，因为老议员们已经表示不参加新议会的竞选。

sentences.en: So these people are even younger than their predecessors, even less experienced, and more likely to not come from Paris, but to come from small towns.
sentences.zh: 所以这些人比他们的前任还要年轻，经验更少，并且大多来自小城镇而非巴黎。

sentences.en: Only a tiny fraction of them live in Paris.
sentences.zh: 只有极少数人住在巴黎。

sentences.en: So they are outsiders.
sentences.zh: 所以他们是不折不扣的外来者。

sentences.en: That's a bit of an obstacle when you're in the middle of this capital, seething with tension.
sentences.zh: 当置身于这个充满紧张气氛的首都时，这算是一个不小的障碍。

sentences.en: Another big handicap for them, they've only been elected by a tiny, tiny turnout.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说另一个巨大的劣势是，他们的当选投票率低得可怜。

sentences.en: So there were sort of strict property thresholds for who could vote.
sentences.zh: 当时对谁有投票权有着严格的财产门槛限制。

sentences.en: And the turnout anyway was terrible.
sentences.zh: 而且投票率本来就很糟糕。

sentences.en: So in some areas, it was only 10%, 11%.
sentences.zh: 所以在有些地区，投票率只有10%、11%。

sentences.en: In Paris, it was only 14%.
sentences.zh: 在巴黎也只有14%。

sentences.en: So actually, they have not got much of a mandate, you would say, not much of a popular mandate.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，你可以说他们并没有获得多少民意授权，没有多少民意基础。

sentences.en: So in they go.
sentences.zh: 于是他们上任了。

sentences.en: And straight away, the factionalism, you were kind of chuckling when I said we were about to introduce the Girondins as a new faction.
sentences.zh: 紧接着，党派之争——当我刚才说我们即将把吉伦特派作为新派系引入时，你还在那儿偷笑——

sentences.en: The factualism starts straight away.
sentences.zh: 派系斗争立刻就开始了。

sentences.en: They arrange themselves very self-consciously.
sentences.zh: 他们非常刻意地划分座位。

sentences.en: The radicals on the left, the more conservative on the right.
sentences.zh: 左翼是激进派，右翼是更保守的派系。

sentences.en: This is obviously the French Revolution, the first time this has ever happened.
sentences.zh: 这显然是法国大革命中的头一遭。

sentences.en: About four out of 10 of them, historians think, are Foyon, moderates, who back Barnard and Co.
sentences.zh: 历史学家认为，其中大约十分之四是斐扬派、温和派，他们支持巴纳夫及同僚。

sentences.en: Another four out of five are in the middle.
sentences.zh: 另外五分之四在中间。

sentences.en: People call them the plain, because they sit in the kind of the bottom of the assembly.
sentences.zh: 人们称他们为平原派，因为他们坐在议会的低处。

sentences.en: And they can be swayed one way or another.
sentences.zh: 他们可以左右摇摆。

sentences.en: And that leaves about two out of 10 maximum who are radicals, members of the Jacquemin club.
sentences.zh: 这就剩下最多十分之二是激进派，也就是雅各宾俱乐部的成员。

sentences.en: And the big difference is not one of background and social class and that stuff.
sentences.zh: 而最大的区别不在于背景、社会阶层这些东西。

sentences.en: It's actually kind of temperaments and ideology.
sentences.zh: 实际上是气质和意识形态的不同。

sentences.en: The Foyon think, basically, anarchy is very dangerous.
sentences.zh: 斐扬派基本上认为，无政府状态非常危险。

sentences.en: The streets are dangerous.
sentences.zh: 街头是危险的。

sentences.en: Moderation is all.
sentences.zh: 温和稳健才是一切。

sentences.en: And the Jacquemin think, the common people are the incarnations of virtue.
sentences.zh: 而雅各宾派则认为，普通老百姓是美德的化身。

sentences.en: Poor people have wisdom and decency that richer people don't have.
sentences.zh: 穷人有着富人所没有的智慧和正直。

sentences.en: And we should embolden them and enfranchise them as much as possible.
sentences.zh: 我们应该尽可能地赋予他们勇气和选举权。

sentences.en: So they're populists.
sentences.zh: 所以他们是民粹主义者。

sentences.en: And this is a reversal of the traditional way of understanding things, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这颠覆了传统的认知方式，对吧？

sentences.en: That it is wealth and education that brings you the expertise that enables you to run a government.
sentences.zh: 传统认为，财富和教育带给你专业知识，从而使你能够管理政府。

sentences.en: And the Robespierre position, the radical Jacquemin position, is that it's precisely the lack of that makes the poor more honest in a kind of Rousseauist manner.
sentences.zh: 而罗伯斯庇尔的立场、激进的雅各宾派立场则是，恰恰是缺乏这些，才以一种卢梭式的方式让穷人显得更加诚实。

sentences.en: They look into their souls and what is written on their souls is worth a million times what people have learned in, you know, salons and so on.
sentences.zh: 他们审视自己的灵魂，灵魂上铭刻的东西，比人们在诸如沙龙之类的地方学到的东西有价值成千上万倍。

sentences.en: So they've obviously got this from Rousseau and Rousseau obviously got it from a bloke in the Middle East in roundabout the turn of, you know, the reign of the Emperor Augustus.
sentences.zh: 所以他们显然是从卢梭那里继承了这一套，而卢梭显然又是从中东的一个家伙那儿学来的，大约是在奥古斯都皇帝统治时期左右，对吧？

sentences.en: Didn't he tell me, is that correct?
sentences.zh: 他没跟我这么说过，是这样吗？

sentences.en: The last should be first and the first should be last and all that kind of business?
sentences.zh: 卑微者将升为至高，尊贵者将降为卑微，诸如此类？

sentences.en: Clearly there are elements of that, yeah.
sentences.zh: 这里面显然有这些成分，对。

sentences.en: So there's this idea.
sentences.zh: 所以有这样一种思想。

sentences.en: I mean, they're all idealistic, by the way, in different ways.
sentences.zh: 我是说，顺便说一句，他们都很理想主义，只是方式不同。

sentences.en: I mean, you could be a moderate or a radical.
sentences.zh: 无论你是温和派还是激进派。

sentences.en: You're still, they're all pretty idealistic.
sentences.zh: 你依然——他们其实都相当理想主义。

sentences.en: But from the moment they sit down, they're facing massive, massive challenges.
sentences.zh: 但从他们落座的那一刻起，他们就面临着极其巨大的挑战。

sentences.en: I mean, France is in an absolute mess.
sentences.zh: 我是说，法兰西当时简直一团糟。

sentences.en: Let's not underestimate that in the autumn of 1791.
sentences.zh: 在1791年秋天，我们绝对不能低估这一点。

sentences.en: Half of the clergy are effectively in open defiance of the civil authorities because they have refused to swear this oath to the civil constitution of the clergy.
sentences.zh: 一半的神职人员实际上都在公开抗命民政当局，因为他们拒绝向《教士公民组织法》宣誓。

sentences.en: Mass eruptions in the countryside, peasants refusing to pay their feudal dues to their seigneur and saying this is completely legitimate and kind of attacking Chateau
sentences.zh: 乡村地区大规模爆发骚乱，农民拒绝向领主缴纳封建租税，并声称这完全合法，甚至攻击城堡

sentences.en: and kind of destroying documents and things.
sentences.zh: 并损毁文件之类的东西。

sentences.en: Hard currency in France by this point has virtually disappeared and the French economy is afloat with paper money, which a lot of people find deeply suspicious and dodgy.
sentences.zh: 此时法兰西的硬币已经几乎绝迹，法国经济全靠纸币支撑，许多人对此深表怀疑和不信任。

sentences.en: I don't trust paper notes.
sentences.zh: 我不信任纸币。

sentences.en: And they're called assignats and they are plummeting in value.
sentences.zh: 这些纸币被称为指券，它们的价值正在暴跌。

sentences.en: So that means prices are going up.
sentences.zh: 这意味着物价正在上涨。

sentences.en: And classically traditions like that foster conspiracy theories, don't they?
sentences.zh: 而这样的传统往往会滋生阴谋论，对吧？

sentences.en: It's all being manipulated by...
sentences.zh: 这一切都是由……在操纵

sentences.en: Speculators.
sentences.zh: 投机者。

sentences.en: Speculators and hoarders.
sentences.zh: 投机商和囤积居奇者。

sentences.en: So that's not helpful either.
sentences.zh: 所以这毫无益处。

sentences.en: Not helpful at all.
sentences.zh: 一点帮助也没有。

sentences.en: And in Paris, there is a growing sense of militancy and disorder because people can't afford to buy bread and people are angry and people have been kind of radicalized
sentences.zh: 在巴黎，激进主义和混乱情绪日益高涨，因为人们买不起面包，人们满腔怒火，并且在过去几年事件的冲击下

sentences.en: by the events of the last couple of years.
sentences.zh: 变得激进化了。

sentences.en: And they have a sense that basically this new Legislative Assembly is meeting, but who gives a hoot about them?
sentences.zh: 他们有一种感觉，基本上就是这个新的立法议会在开会，但谁特么在乎他们？

sentences.en: They don't really represent me anyway.
sentences.zh: 反正他们也代表不了我。

sentences.en: So there's all that.
sentences.zh: 所以情况就是这样。

sentences.en: Now on top of that, there is something else we mentioned last time, which is that when the Legislative Assembly meets, for the first time the news has actually arrived in France
sentences.zh: 除此之外，还有我们上次提到过的另一件事，那就是当立法议会召开时，法国第一次真正收到了这样的消息：

sentences.en: that the slaves on Saint-Domingue have launched a massive uprising in the richest colony empire.
sentences.zh: 圣多明各的奴隶们在这个帝国最富裕的殖民地上发动了大规模起义。

sentences.en: This is a huge challenge for France, for its economy, but also, as you said, Tom, what do you do if you've committed yourself to the rights of man,
sentences.zh: 这对法国及其经济来说是个巨大的挑战，但正如你所说，汤姆，如果你既致力于人权，

sentences.en: but at the same time you believe in the rights of property and the importance of order?
sentences.zh: 但同时又信仰财产权和秩序的重要性，那你该怎么办？

sentences.en: And you also believe in preserving the French economy.
